sentences.text: Assailing the order dated 02/03.01.2013 passed by the respondent No.2 rejecting the claim of the petitioner holding that the case of the petitioner cannot be considered for extending the benefit of the policy of the State Government, the present writ petition has been filed.
2. It is the case of the petitioner that one Deba Patel was having three sons, who were having 1/3rd share in the property.
The properties were jointly recorded in their names in the revenue records.
The said property was required for development and construction of Power Grid Corporation Satna in the year 1997.
The compensation was awarded to the land oustees.
The land of the petitioner was taken up for the construction of Power Grid Corporation and along with compensation, a commitment was made to grant employment to atleast one person of the family.

On 06-07-2011,
after attaining the age of majority, the petitioner filed an application requesting NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18202 2 WP-12756-2013 that the case of the petitioner be considered for employment enclosing the documents i.e. 10+2 HSSC certificate of the year 2004.
His father was called upon to submit an affidavit before the authority concerned, which was submitted by his father.

3. When the case of the petitioner was not considered, he made a representation for providing Sugreev Prasad Patel vs Powergrid Corporation Of India Ltd. on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197582437/
1 employment in pursuance to the policy, which is consistently followed by the respondents.

sentences.text: As the application was kept pending, he filed a writ petition before this court being W.P.No.2607 of 2012 (S), which was disposed off vide order dated 19-03-2012 with a direction to the respondents to consider and decide the claim of the petitioner in pursuance to the policy formulated by the respondents within a period of two months and communicate the result to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 communicated the decision to the petitioner informing that the Power Grid Corporation is not having any such scheme for providing employment to land oustees.

It is pointed out that the Satna Sub Station Power Grid has not given any undertaking for giving employment to all 17 land oustees, but only 5 poorest of poor land oustees of Satna whose names were forwarded by the district authorities, have already been provided employment after due consideration.
4. It is the case of the petitioner that land of some other persons were also acquired and the employment to one of the family member of the land oustees were provided and some were left out.

Two similarly situated persons namely Awadhesh Dubey and Jeyut Bandhan Ram Vishwakarma filed a writ petition and thereafter contempt petition before the Court and in NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18202 3 WP-12756-2013 pursuance to the directions given in the writ petition and during the pendency of the contempt petition, the meeting of Board of Directors of Power Grid Corporation was held on 09.09.2009 and a decision was taken in respect of remaining 7 land oustees including Awadhesh Dubey and Jeyut Bandhan Ram Vishwakarma for their appointment.
The petitioner is a similarly situated.

The decision taken by the authorities dated 30.05.2012 was subject matter of challenge in the Writ Petition No.12227 of 2012 which was disposed off on 17.08.2012 with the direction to the respondents to reconsider the case of the petitioner and to inquire into the financial status and if the case of the petitioner is found at par with those other persons who have been granted employment, necessary orders be passed by the respondents taking a sympathetic view in the matter.
The petitioner again made a detailed representation.

Thereafter the order impugned has been passed by the authorities rejecting the claim of the petitioner on the similar ground that they were required to give employment to only 5 persons who were poorest of poor and to those whose names were recommended by the District Collector, Satna.

As the name of the petitioner was never recommended by the Collector, therefore,
the request of the petitioner for providing employment could not have been considered.

It is argued before this Court that there was a specific direction in the second round of litigation by this Court directing the respondent No.2 to examine financial status of the petitioner with those persons who have been provided employment and thereafter necessary orders to be passed.
The said exercise is not carried out by the authorities and they have passed the impugned order.
Therefore, this NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18202 4 WP-12756-2013 petition.
5. On notice being issued, a reply has been filed by the respondent Nos.1 to 3.
They have denied the petition's averments.
A preliminary objection is taken that the Power Grid Corporation is not having any scheme or policy for providing employment to land oustees.

For the purpose of construction of 400 KV /220 KV Satna and a residential complex, an extent of 61.934 hectare of the land was acquired by the Madhya Pradesh State Government as per the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act and persons whose land was acquired have been given adequate compensation by the respondents.

During the aforesaid proceedings, an agreement was entered into between the State Government and the Power Grid wherein in terms of clause 4, they have agreed that out of 17 land Sugreev Prasad Patel vs Powergrid Corporation Of India Ltd. on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/197582437/
2 owners, 5 poorest of poor land owners or any other member of the family should be given employment in the Power Grid.

sentences.text: For the said purpose, the Collector, Satna was required to assess the financial status of all the land owners and finally select 5 poorest of poor persons as per the said agreement.
Five poorest of poor persons were selected by the Collector and a list of those persons was forwarded to the Power Grid vide letter dated 15-03-2000 for granting employment in Power Grid.
On the date when the list of eligible candidates was forwarded, the petitioner was a minor aged about 12 years.
He has passed his high school certificate examination in the year 2004.
Thus, there was no occasion for the Power Grid to consider the case of the petitioner at the relevant time.

The petitioner was neither having minimum qualification nor he was eligible in terms of the age for the purpose of grant of employment in the Power Grid in NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:18202 5 WP-12756-2013 the year 2000.

The respondents/Power Grid authorities have given employment to 5 poorest of poor land owners in terms of the list forwarded by the Collector and they have complied with clause 4 of the said agreement.
It is contended that the agreement dated 26-06-1997 cannot be kept in motion for years together particularly when the appointment of all eligible candidates was already made the year 2000.
The petitioner has not challenged the appointment of any of the persons who have been granted employment by the respondents.
It is submitted that in view of the direction given by this Court, the case of the petitioner was reconsidered by the authorities and his claim was rejected.
They have prayed for dismissal of the writ petition.

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
7.

The admitted facts of the case are that the land of the 17 persons was acquired for the construction of Power Grid by the State Government and adequate compensation has been paid to all the land oustees.

As per the Clause 4 of the agreement entered into between the State Government as well as the Power Grid, the Power Grid were required to grant employment to 5 poorest of poor persons which are required to be identified by the Collector.

The Collector after an enquiry has identified 5 poorest of poor persons and forwarded the list to the respondent/Power Grid who has considered the same and granted appointment to those 5 persons in the year 2000.
The petitioner at the relevant time was a minor aged about 12 years who was not even qualified for grant of any employment.
However, in terms of the directions given by the Court, his case was again considered by the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:18202 6 WP-12756-2013 authorities and rejected his claim.
The entire drive of granting appointment to 5 poorest of poor persons was completed way back in the year 2000.

As for the petitioner himself, on attaining majority, he has submitted an application for grant of appointment on 06-07-2011 i.e. almost after a period of 10 years from the date of employment granted to 5 other persons.

The petitioner cannot seek similarity with those who have been granted employment because at the relevant time when employment was granted, the petitioner was not eligible to enter into the service because he was a minor.
He has completed his high school examination in the year 2004.
There is no challenge made by the petitioner to the orders granting employment to five others persons by the respondent/Power Grid.
The agreement dated 26.06.1997 cannot be kept open for years together particularly when the respondents have already granted appointment to five poorest persons way back in the year 2000.
Therefore, no relief can be extended to the petitioner.
